title: Dashboard rollout snapshot and trace orchestration notes
content:
Purpose and context

This note captures a compact, operationally-focused plan for: (1) capturing dashboard snapshots tied to rollouts and canaries, (2) coordinating trace sampling and orchestration during rollout windows, and (3) a teardown checklist that preserves investigation artifacts and cost constraints. Intended audience: oncall, release engineers running canaries, and observability stewards.

Goals
- Ensure rollouts include an immutable telemetry snapshot for SLI/alert replays.
- Keep tracing during rollouts targeted and cheap while preserving high-value span anchors for root cause.
- Provide a lightweight dashboard layout and a teardown runbook that conserves query budget.

High-level approach
1) At rollout start: capture SLI snapshot (metric set + quantiles) for baseline.
2) Increase trace sampling for rollout cohort only (session-sliced sampling) + preserve span anchors for all errors.
3) Maintain dashboard light-mode (compact panels) with cost-aware query windows.
4) On teardown: store snapshot artifacts (JSON) and instrument a short-term extended retention for traces tied to the cohort id.

Signal inventory (metric definitions to snapshot)
- inference.request.count | unit: requests/min | agg: sum over 1m | owner: eng-serving-runtime | alert: sustained drop > 30% vs snapshot baseline (10m)
- inference.ttft.total_p95_ms | unit: ms | agg: 95th quantile over 1m | owner: eng-observability | alert: increase > 40% vs baseline
- inference.kv.warmth_ratio | unit: ratio (0-1) | agg: avg over 1m | owner: serving-runtime | alert: < 0.5 for 5m during high traffic
- inference.embedding.latency_p90_ms | unit: ms | agg: 90th quantile | owner: eng-serving-runtime | notes: snapshot for model-variant cohorts
- infra.gpu.utilization_pct | unit: % | agg: avg over 1m | owner: platform-engineering | alert: sustained > 85%
- cost.query_eu_credits | unit: currency/credits | agg: sum per hour | owner: finance | alert: projected hourly > threshold

Each metric in the snapshot: record value, aggregation window, and tagging (cohort-id, rollout-id, model-variant). Store as immutable JSON in artifact store with path convention: s3://obs-snapshots/{rollout-id}/{timestamp}.json

Tracing: span design and sampling policy for rollouts
- Principle: keep traces small but semantically rich — prioritize span anchors (authorization, routing decision, model-invoke) and error spans.
- Span naming convention during rollouts: "rr:{route}:{step}" (rr = rollout-run). Example: rr/chat/route-select, rr/chat/model-invoke, rr/chat/kv-lookup.
- Required span tags to preserve: cohort_id, rollout_id, model_variant, tenant_id, request_token_count, backend_node_id, kv_hit:true/false, fallback_reason.
- Sampling strategy: session-sliced sampling + spike capture
  - Default: 0.5% global sample (keep baseline cost low)
  - Rollout cohort: 10% session sample (samples tied to cohort_id header)
  - Error override: 100% sampling for traces with spans flagged error=true or latency_ms > (p95 * 2)
  - Anchor preservation: always retain root + first model-invoke span and its immediate two children for sampled sessions to aid causal chains
- Trace orchestration knobs to expose in release: sampling_multiplier, cohort_header_name (X-Rollout-ID), error_latency_threshold_ms

Dashboard composition and compact-mode guidelines
- Compose a single compact dashboard for rollouts with 6 panels max: global SLI snapshot row (3 panels), cohort-level breakdown row (2 panels), anomaly/alerts row (1 panel).
- Panel queries should be time-bounded to rollout window by default (rollout.start to now) and cachable snapshots for historical comparisons.
- Use derived lightweight metrics instead of raw high-cardinality ones where possible (e.g., pre-aggregated tenant_slices).
- Dashboard controls: rollout dropdown (rollout-id), cohort switch, time scrubber pegged to rollout start
- Query cost guardrails: ban unbounded GROUP BY tenant_id across full retention in dashboard panels — require explicit cohort or limit to top-10 tenants.

Canary snapshot + teardown runbook (step-by-step)
1) Pre-rollout (15–60m before): create snapshot-id -> run artifact snapshot: metrics list + current SLI baselines. Upload artifact.
   - Command: obsctl snapshot create --rollout $ROLLOUT_ID --metrics metrics-list.json --out s3://obs-snapshots/$ROLLOUT_ID/$TS.json
2) Rollout start: add header X-Rollout-ID to traffic router for cohort. Enable cohort sampling multiplier.
   - Command: releasectl rollout start --id $ROLLOUT_ID --cohort-percent 10 --headers "X-Rollout-ID:$ROLLOUT_ID"
3) During rollout (first 30–120m): monitor compact dashboard, watch: ttft_p95, kv_warmth, error_rate, cost.query_eu_credits.
4) Spike detection: if p95 doubles or error_rate > threshold for 5 consecutive buckets -> trigger fast rollback and mark traces for extended retention.
5) Teardown (successful or rollback): capture post-rollout snapshot (same metric set), mark snapshot artifacts: pre, during, post. Freeze cohort traces: set retention-tier extended for traces with tag rollout_id=$ROLLOUT_ID for 7d (cost-guarded).
   - Command: obsctl retention set --tag rollout_id=$ROLLOUT_ID --tier extended --duration 7d
6) Post-mortem artifacts: store dashboard permalink, snapshot JSONs, and a trace sample list (trace ids) to the incident folder.

Investigation checklist (short)
- Validate snapshot timestamps and tag integrity (cohort_id present).
- Compare pre/during/post quantiles side-by-side.
- Rehydrate a sampled trace chain: verify span anchors exist (routing -> model_invoke -> kv).
- If missing span anchors, search by request_token_count and tenant_id to correlate sessions.
- Export top anomalous traces (by latency and errors) as ndjson for offline analysis.

Cost and retention rules (practical defaults)
- Traces: baseline retention 7d; cohort traces elevated to 7d only if rollout > 5% traffic or triggered rollback; otherwise 72h.
- Snapshots: always archived indefinitely in compressed JSON (cheap).
- Dashboard queries: prefer pre-aggregated metrics endpoint; disallow expensive ad-hoc queries on primary dashboards during rollouts.

Open questions and action items
- Decide default cohort sampling percent for 1st-pass rollouts (proposal: 5% by default, 10% for high-risk). Owner: Priya.
- Add a small obsctl command to auto-generate the dashboard permalink and attach snapshot artifacts to JIRA. Owner: Miguel.
- Run a cost simulation for extended trace retention vs. benefit of root-cause fidelity. Owner: Finance + Observability.

Appendix: quick reference values
- Default rollout sampling: 10% (cohort) / 0.5% (global) / error override 100%
- Snapshot artifact path: s3://obs-snapshots/{rollout-id}/{ts}.json
- Required span tags: cohort_id, rollout_id, model_variant, tenant_id, request_token_count
- Deck shortname for handoff: obs-roll-snapshots

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep dashboard panels minimal — operators need speed.
- When in doubt, preserve span anchors and not every internal span.
- This is intentionally opinionated: aim for cheap traces + high signal fidelity for rollouts.
